source.title: Scaling Capability in Token Space: An Analysis of Large Vision Language Model
source.authors: Tenghui Li; Guo-Xu Zhou; Xu-Yang Zhao; Qi-Bin Zhao

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether scaling-like performance trends occur when varying vision-token count in a vision-language model, a new modality and setting relative to language-model pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study fits benchmark performance against vision-token count and reports fitted coefficients. Its hidden-state divergence analysis is a proxy for discriminative capacity, not held-out pretraining loss, so it is not recorded as a result for the claim versions. Cited language-model scaling findings and baseline-model comparisons are not study results for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits downstream benchmark scores against the number of visual tokens supplied per image to a fixed language-model backbone. These tokens are input representations, not training-data tokens. It does not measure loss scaling with parameters, training data or training compute, or downstream predictability from those quantities. Its fitted exponents and outlier sensitivity concern this different relationship, so they do not test V5 or V7 as extensions or qualifications of the stated training scaling laws.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their divergence framework predicts visual-token scaling regimes and that benchmark scores approximately follow the proposed relationship. They acknowledge limited generalizability from one vision-language architecture and attribute RealWorldQA deviations to answer formatting. Their theoretical bridge from divergence to task performance is a hypothesis, rather than an independently established equivalence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a custom vision-language model and varies vision-token count, fitting downstream benchmark scores; it does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy against parameters, training tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted c and α vary across benchmarks and between the Vision Question Queries and Vision Queries (ft) input configurations. RealWorldQA fit changes when the n_l=384 and n_l=512 anomalous points are excluded.

fits_no_version.finding: Across ten visual-token configurations from 1 to 768, most benchmark scores are described as approximately following S(n)=c/n^alpha. Coefficients vary by benchmark and by whether questions enter the fusion module. No fit-quality statistics or held-out extrapolation tests are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this fine-tuned vision-language architecture, downstream scores can often be approximated by a power law in the number of fused visual input tokens per image.

fits_no_version.finding: RealWorldQA fits are disrupted by response-formatting failures, especially without question-conditioned fusion; removing the 384- and 512-token points improves the reported fits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Score-versus-visual-input-token fits can depend on response parsing, adaptation and post-hoc point exclusion.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 3.5–3.6 derive a hidden-state divergence bound with square-root and linear regimes and compare a fitted version with divergence measurements on paired text answers across several LLMs. Performance proportionality to divergence is hypothesized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cumulative hidden-state divergence between paired sequences can be approximated using sequence length and representation correlations.

record.problems: Empirical validation uses one custom architecture and the authors acknowledge that its specific parameters may not generalize. Several fits are described as imperfect; RealWorldQA has formatting-related anomalies. The token-count experiments reuse a model trained with nl=256 and ns=8, then fine-tune alternatives on 10% of the data. The study evaluates downstream task scores, not held-out pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: The raw score at every token count for all benchmarks and the question-inclusion performance-difference plots in Figures 9-13 and Tables 2-4 were not transcribed individually; the 60-row limit was avoided by recording the fitted benchmark summaries and the reported RealWorldQA exceptions. Baseline-model comparisons and computational-cost results are not results for the claim versions.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, training tokens or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on small runs; all reported benchmark fits use the evaluated configurations.
Loss-minimising parameter and training-token allocations at fixed training compute.
Depth, width and architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Extension of training-loss power laws to other modalities or training regimes. The study varies visual input compression and fits task scores instead.
Downstream predictability from model/training scale or pretraining loss. Visual input-token count is the varied quantity here.
Setup and fitting dependence of training scaling exponents, compute-optimal splits and disagreements between published training laws.

record.verdict_notes: Judgment uses only the supplied text. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions, not judgments that the reported benchmark scores are unreadable. The backbone is frozen; alternative token configurations reuse a base trained at n_l=256, n_s=8 and receive further training on 10% of the data. Fitting a power-law function alone does not establish predictive accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
Does not fit loss curves on small language-model runs and test predictions on much larger runs.
Does not vary model parameters and training tokens at fixed compute or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests benchmark performance versus vision-token count in one model architecture. Does not test image/video models generally, audio, repeated data, or transfer regimes as such.
Measures downstream benchmark performance against vision-token count, not against model scale or pretraining loss.

Shows variation by benchmark and input configuration, and an anomalous benchmark fit. Does not directly compare published language-model exponents, parameter-counting choices, compute-optimal splits, or alternative fitting methods.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Benchmarks other than RealWorldQA, in both reported input configurations
reader_labels.reason: The fitted benchmark trends are described as capturing performance variation with vision-token count; see S01-S09, S11-S18, S19-S27, and S29-S36.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RealWorldQA, especially the reported n_l=384 and n_l=512 points
reader_labels.reason: The original fit was disrupted by formatting-related score drops; the authors report improved fits after removing those points, so adherence was not uniform across all tested settings (S10, S28, S37-S42).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Across benchmarks and the two input configurations
reader_labels.reason: The fitted exponents differ across benchmarks and between the question-included and further-fine-tuned configurations, showing setup- and task-dependent fitted scaling parameters (S01-S36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RealWorldQA fitting with all token-count points included
reader_labels.reason: The text reports failure of the original fit because of formatting anomalies, while stating that removing the affected points improved fit consistency (S10, S28, S37-S42).
